The existing switch is a big live-transport implementation. Given the contract's complexity and precision, I think the most reliable approach is to write a fresh, careful C implementation of the collector (or possibly Python, but performance matters: up to 2^20 work units per batch, 120 seconds; Python could handle it but C is safer... Actually, let's think: work units include per-packet processing plus snapshots costing N each and retries costing 12N+4. With N up to 4096 and D up to 1024, a pure-Python implementation could be slow but maybe OK. However, traffic budget 256 MiB with 4x frame lengths means up to 64 MiB of frames. Building frames in Python for millions of packets is feasible-ish but slow (maybe ~50-100 µs each → 1M packets = 100s, too slow). So C is the right choice.
